raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Single-GPU decode batches can exceed the default CUDA graph ceiling while ample GPU memory remains. Those batches fall back to eager execution, which is expensive for CPU-bound decode workloads.

## Modifications

- With default graph and memory settings, extend decode coverage to 512 requests above 60 GiB and 256 at 35–60 GiB. Charge the additional graphs to the static memory reserve and preserve the existing running-request limit.
- Respect explicit graph/memory choices and exclude configurations the planner does not model, including multi-GPU, speculative decode, dLLMs, hybrid models, multimodal models, and LoRA.
- Keep post-capture KV sizing opt-in. For that mode, bound the default running batch by captured graph sizes, back off on small KV budgets, and reserve sampling state, decode/prefill tails, and allocator fragmentation.
- Add `SGLANG_ENABLE_DECODE_GRAPH_PLANNER=0` to restore the existing graph tier; document the defaults and opt-in behavior.

Related work: [#43645](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43645) accounts for the request-token table in the pre-capture budget; this changes graph coverage and its reserve. [#45608](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45608) addresses a prefill coverage gap for post-capture sizing; this preserves the existing eligibility gate.

## Accuracy Tests

Added CPU tests for full argument-resolution precedence, supported GPU tiers and exclusion gates, reserve sizing, request-cap backoff, and post-capture headroom.

Local validation against current main on macOS: `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_runtime_reserve.py -q` passed all 5 tests. The full argument-resolution suite cannot complete in this environment: its simulated CUDA platform reaches `cutlass_fp8_supported()` without a CUDA device capability (`None >= 9`), also reproduced on unmodified upstream main. All applicable pinned pre-commit hooks pass, including formatting, Python parsing, and indirect-import validation. Linux/CUDA validation remains required.

`PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_kv_canary_headroom.py test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_pool_configurator.py -q` also passed **77 tests and 48 subtests** locally.

Historical validation supplied with the patch, against `99fd01047d67bb249641a8e50282a1a5218afc63`: 106 focused tests and 56 subtests passed on an A10G environment. H100 greedy outputs matched 64/64; L40S matched 56/64 when the base used eager decode and the patch used CUDA graphs. This is not a claim of bitwise equivalence across execution modes. Worst-sampling, input-logprob, and overlapped-load gates completed all requests without hard OOMs; allocator retries were reported separately.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Historical same-host measurements supplied with the patch; these were not rerun during this PR preparation. Each result below has one base and one patch measurement. Both arms use default server flags.

| GPU / model / workload | Base output tok/s | Patch output tok/s | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| H100 / Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 / 1024-in, 256-out, c384 | 3,478 | 6,767 | +94.6% |
| H100 / Qwen3-8B / 256-in, 256-out, c512 | 11,100 | 13,471 | +21.4% |
| L40S / Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 / 1024-in, 256-out, c128 | 798 | 995 | +24.7% |
| L40S / Qwen3-8B / 128-in, 128-out, c1024, non-streaming | 4,722 | 4,695 | -0.6% |

The additional graph reserve reduces KV capacity by roughly 1.1–1.5% on the H100 models and 2.0–5.6% on the L40S models listed above. The last workload had a 38.3% higher median TTFT, despite nearly unchanged throughput. Startup also captures additional graphs. Other model families and GPU tiers need wider validation.

Post-capture sizing remains opt-in: its overlapped stress tests exhibited allocator retries, including on the base implementation, and its tighter running cap can reduce throughput for large resident batches.

To reproduce the primary H100 workload, start the server on the base or patch checkout:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 --port 30000
```

In a separate terminal, run the same client against each arm, with the planner and post-capture environment overrides unset:

```bash
python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 1152 --max-concurrency 384
```

## Checklist

- [x] Complete pinned pre-commit checks.
- [x] Add focused CPU regression tests with CI registration.
- [x] Update the tuning documentation.
- [x] Provide historical accuracy and speed results with limitations.
- [ ] Run relevant Linux/CUDA CI on the current base.

Prepared with AI assistance (Codex); local checks and supplied historical measurements are distinguished above.

@@ -65,10 +65,15 @@ If you encounter out-of-memory (OOM) errors, you can adjust the following parame
 - You can also reduce `--mem-fraction-static` to a smaller value, such as 0.8 or 0.7. This decreases the memory usage of the KV cache memory pool and helps prevent OOM errors during both prefill and decoding. However, it limits maximum concurrency and reduces peak throughput.
 
 ### Tune `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`
-By default, CUDA graph is enabled only for small batch sizes (e.g., less than 160 or 256).
+On a single NVIDIA GPU, eligible text-generation models without hybrid state, speculative or diffusion decoding, or LoRA receive wider decode CUDA graph coverage when you leave `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` and `--mem-fraction-static` unset: up to 512 requests on GPUs with more than 60 GB (for example an 80 GB H100), and up to 256 on 35 to 60 GB GPUs (for example an L40S). The running limit is unchanged, so larger decode batches still run eagerly, and the static memory reserve grows by the memory of the extra graphs, exactly as it would with the matching explicit `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`. With an explicit `--max-running-requests` below that ceiling, the graphs cover up to the limit, so every decode batch is graphed. Models with custom memory overrides or unsupported graph-capture configurations keep the existing plan. Set `SGLANG_ENABLE_DECODE_GRAPH_PLANNER=0` to restore the tier defaults.
+
+With `SGLANG_ENABLE_POST_CAPTURE_KV_SIZING=1`, the KV cache pool is sized from the GPU memory left after graph capture instead. On a single GPU, decode CUDA graphs then cover up to 512 requests and the default running batch is capped at the largest captured graph, so no decode step falls back to the slower eager path because of its batch size, and the pool keeps a reserve for that batch's sampling state, the eager decode and prefill tails and allocator fragmentation. Where that reserve for 512 requests would exceed a tenth of the KV cache budget (a large model on the GPU), the cap backs off to a smaller captured size; the startup log reports the final `max_running_requests`.
+
+In other configurations (for example multiple GPUs, speculative decoding or diffusion LLMs), CUDA graph is enabled only for small batch sizes by default (e.g., less than 160 or 256).
 However, for some models, especially at large tensor parallelism sizes, CUDA graph can be useful for batch sizes up to 512 or 768.
 Therefore, it may be beneficial to increase `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` to a larger value.
 Note that CUDA graph consumes more memory, so you may need to reduce `--mem-fraction-static` at the same time.
+An explicit `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` keeps its exact meaning: decode batches above the captured size still run eagerly.
 
 ### Tune `--dp-size` and `--tp-size`

+def _derived_mem_fraction_static(server_args: Any, gpu_mem: Optional[float]) -> float:
+    cfg = resolving_view(server_args)
+    model_config = model_config_of(server_args)
+    is_vlm = (
+        model_config.is_multimodal
+        and not cfg.language_only
+        and not cfg.language_model_only
+        and cfg.disaggregation_mode != "decode"
+    )
+    post_capture_kv_sizing = post_capture_kv_sizing_planned(server_args)
+
+    if post_capture_kv_sizing:
+        # Post-capture sizing measures free memory after graph capture, so
+        # skip the graph/activation reserve; keep only the floor + parallel slack.
+        reserved_mem = 1536
+        reserved_mem += cfg.tp_size * cfg.pp_size / 8 * 1024
+    else:
+        # Tokens the activation working set scales with (per serving mode).
+        if cfg.disaggregation_mode == "decode":
+            running_requests = (
+                cfg.max_running_requests or cfg.cuda_graph_config.decode.max_bs or 1
+            )
+            draft_tokens = cfg.speculative_num_draft_tokens or 1
+            activation_tokens = max(running_requests * draft_tokens, 2048)
+        elif cfg.chunked_prefill_size > 0:
+            activation_tokens = max(cfg.chunked_prefill_size, 2048)
+        else:
+            activation_tokens = max(cfg.max_prefill_tokens, 2048)
+        # Constant meta data (e.g., from attention backend) + activation slack.
+        reserved_mem = 512
+        reserved_mem += activation_tokens * 1.5

+        reserved_mem += cfg.tp_size * cfg.pp_size / 8 * 1024

+        if gpu_mem is not None and gpu_mem > 60 * 1024:
+            reserved_mem = max(reserved_mem, 10 * 1024)
+        # Reserve headroom for DeepEP all-to-all buffers on top of the floor.
+        reserved_mem += reserve_for_deepep_a2a_mb(server_args)
+        # XPU: oneDNN allocates scratch space for matmul when
+        # M is not a power-of-2-aligned value (e.g. M=2100).  Reserve extra
+        # headroom so non-aligned prefill lengths don't hit OOM.
+        if get_platform().is_xpu:
+            reserved_mem += 2 * 1024
+
+    mem_fraction_static = (
+        round((gpu_mem - reserved_mem) / gpu_mem, 3) if gpu_mem is not None else 0.95
+    )
+
+    # Multimodal models need more memory for the image processing.
+    if is_vlm:
+        mem_fraction_static = adjust_mem_fraction_for_vlm(
+            mem_fraction_static,
+            model_config,
+            post_capture_kv_sizing,
+            gpu_mem,
+        )
+    return mem_fraction_static
+
+
+def plan_decode_graph_coverage(server_args: Any) -> None:
+    """Raise single-GPU decode CUDA graph coverage above the GPU-tier ceiling.
+
+    By default the plan stays static: the running limit is kept and the extra
+    graphs are charged to the static reserve, as an explicit
+    --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode would. With SGLANG_ENABLE_POST_CAPTURE_KV_SIZING
+    the pool is sized from free memory measured after capture: graphs cover 512
+    requests and the default running batch is capped there, so no decode step runs
+    eagerly and the runtime reserve is bounded by the cap; the KV configurator
+    backs the cap off on a small pool. Runs after every other handler, so each
+    gate reads the final configuration.
+    """
+    cfg = resolving_view(server_args)
+    gpu_mem = get_device_memory_capacity(cfg.device)
+    if not _decode_graph_coverage_applies(server_args, gpu_mem):
+        return
+    measured = envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_POST_CAPTURE_KV_SIZING.get()
+    if measured:
+        ceiling = _PLANNED_DECODE_MAX_BS
+    else:
+        ceiling = _static_plan_decode_max_bs(
+            gpu_mem=gpu_mem, tier_max_bs=cfg.cuda_graph_config.decode.max_bs
+        )
+    if cfg.max_running_requests is not None:
+        ceiling = min(ceiling, cfg.max_running_requests)
+    if ceiling <= cfg.cuda_graph_config.decode.max_bs and not measured:
+        return
+    if ceiling > cfg.cuda_graph_config.decode.max_bs:
+        _declare_decode_graph_ceiling(server_args, ceiling)
+    capped = measured and cfg.max_running_requests is None
+    if capped:
+        declare_resolution(
+            server_args, "plan_decode_graph_coverage", _decode_graph_running_cap=ceiling
+        )
+    # For the graphs a static plan now captures, or for the post-capture floor.
+    declare_resolution(
+        server_args,
+        "plan_decode_graph_coverage",
+        mem_fraction_static=_derived_mem_fraction_static(server_args, gpu_mem),
+    )
+    logger.info(
+        "Decode graph planner: CUDA graphs up to %d requests, %s, KV pool sized %s "
+        "graph capture.",
+        ceiling,
+        "default running batch capped there" if capped else "running limit unchanged",
+        "after" if measured else "before",
+    )
+
+
+def _decode_graph_coverage_applies(server_args: Any, gpu_mem: Optional[float]) -> bool:
+    """Single-GPU CUDA serving with default decode-graph and memory settings, on a
+    model whose KV pool can be sized after capture; the rest keep the tier plan."""
+    cfg = resolving_view(server_args)
+    if gpu_mem is None or gpu_mem < 20 * 1024 or not get_platform().is_cuda:
+        return False
+    if not envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_DECODE_GRAPH_PLANNER.get():
+        return False
+    single_gpu = (
+        cfg.tp_size == 1
+        and cfg.pp_size == 1
+        and cfg.dp_size == 1
+        and not attn_dp_enabled_of(resolved_view(server_args))
+        and cfg.disaggregation_mode == "null"
+        and cfg.moe_a2a_backend == "none"
+    )
+    locked = server_args._cuda_graph_config_locked
+    default_decode_graph = (
+        cfg.cuda_graph_config.decode.backend == Backend.FULL
+        and (Phase.DECODE, "max_bs") not in locked
+        and (Phase.DECODE, "bs") not in locked
+        and not cfg.disable_cuda_graph_padding

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Byte model for runtime memory that lives outside the KV pool and graph memory.
+
+Post-capture KV sizing measures everything allocated by the end of graph capture.
+What it cannot see are the per-step allocations of serving: the sampling state the
+running batch keeps across steps, and the eager tails of the decode and prefill
+forwards. The reserve covers the worst legal combination of them, so it is bounded by
+the running batch size and the prefill chunk size rather than by the request mix.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Optional, Sequence
+
+import msgspec
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
+_FP32_BYTES = 4
+
+# fp32 [num_requests, vocab] rows the running batch keeps across steps: 4 penalizer
+# states (frequency, presence, repetition, min_new_tokens), 6 penalty accumulators
+# (additive and scaling sums of up to three forward copies the overlap scheduler
+# keeps alive) and 1 logit_bias.
+_PERSISTENT_FP32_ROWS = 11
+
+# fp32 [num_requests, vocab] rows a decode step adds: eager-decode logits plus the
+# two min-p renormalizations, or log-probs.
+_DECODE_FP32_ROWS = 3
+
+# Allocator slack and lazily grown workspaces; arbitrary.
+_TRANSIENT_SLACK_BYTES = 1 << 30
+
+# Arbitrary: per-request reserves may claim at most 1/10 of the KV budget before the
+# running cap backs off below the decode graph ceiling.
+_KV_BUDGET_SHARE_DENOMINATOR = 10
+
+
+class TransientReserve(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True, kw_only=True):
+    persistent_bytes: int
+    decode_bytes: int
+    prefill_bytes: int
+    fragmentation_bytes: int
+
+    @property
+    def total_bytes(self) -> int:
+        # Prefill and decode forwards run one at a time, but under interleaving the
+        # caching allocator splits the blocks one tail freed for the other's
+        # tensors, so both tails stay reserved beside the batch's sampling state.
+        return (
+            self.persistent_bytes
+            + self.decode_bytes
+            + self.prefill_bytes
+            + self.fragmentation_bytes
+            + _TRANSIENT_SLACK_BYTES
+        )
+
+
+def transient_reserve(
+    *,
+    vocab_size: int,
+    max_running_requests: int,
+    chunked_prefill_size: Optional[int],
+    enable_deterministic_inference: bool,
+    prefill_graph_bytes: int,
+) -> TransientReserve:
+    """``prefill_graph_bytes`` is the measured prefill graph pool, which bounds an
+    eager forward of one chunk."""
+    row_bytes = _FP32_BYTES * vocab_size
+    logprob_tokens = max(chunked_prefill_size or 0, 0)
+    if envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_LOGPROB_CHUNK.get():
+        logprob_tokens = min(logprob_tokens, envs.SGLANG_LOGPROB_CHUNK_SIZE.get())
+    # The input-logprob tail holds the chunk's fp32 logits and the gathered logprob
+    # rows, plus their log-softmax off the fast path.
+    full_log_softmax = (
+        not envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_FAST_INPUT_LOGPROBS.get()
+        or enable_deterministic_inference
+    )
+    logprob_rows = 3 if full_log_softmax else 2
+    return TransientReserve(
+        persistent_bytes=_PERSISTENT_FP32_ROWS * row_bytes * max_running_requests,
+        decode_bytes=_DECODE_FP32_ROWS * row_bytes * max_running_requests,
+        prefill_bytes=max(
+            prefill_graph_bytes, logprob_rows * row_bytes * logprob_tokens
+        ),
+        # A freed tail block that smaller live tensors split stays reserved, so the
+        # next tail needs one more block of the largest tail allocation.
+        fragmentation_bytes=row_bytes * max(max_running_requests, logprob_tokens),
+    )
+
+
+def graph_bounded_running_cap(
+    *,
+    ceiling: int,
+    capture_bs: Sequence[int],
+    kv_budget_bytes: int,
+    vocab_size: int,
+    context_len: int,
+    page_size: int,
+) -> int:
+    """Largest decode capture size up to ``ceiling`` whose per-request reserve, the
+    sampling state and decode tail plus its graph state, fits in 1/10 of the KV
+    budget."""
+    # Graph state per request: one shared fp32 logits row and one attention index
+    # row, counted as int64 to cover the triton backend.
+    graph_state_bytes = _FP32_BYTES * vocab_size + 8 * -(-context_len // page_size)
+    per_request_bytes = (
+        _PERSISTENT_FP32_ROWS + _DECODE_FP32_ROWS
+    ) * _FP32_BYTES * vocab_size + graph_state_bytes
+    fit = kv_budget_bytes // (_KV_BUDGET_SHARE_DENOMINATOR * per_request_bytes)
+    limit = min(ceiling, fit)
+    return max((bs for bs in capture_bs if bs <= limit), default=min(capture_bs))

+"""The runtime reserve covers what graph capture cannot measure, and the decode
+graph running cap backs off only when that reserve would crowd the KV pool."""
+
+import unittest
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.runtime_reserve import (
+    graph_bounded_running_cap,
+    transient_reserve,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+_GIB = 1 << 30
+_QWEN3_VOCAB = 151936
+_QWEN3_CONTEXT = 40960
+# The decode buckets the planner captures up to 512.
+_CAPTURE_BS = (
+    [1, 2, 4, 8, 12] + list(range(16, 257, 8)) + list(range(272, 512, 16)) + [512]
+)
+
+
+def _cap(kv_budget_gib, *, vocab=_QWEN3_VOCAB):
+    return graph_bounded_running_cap(
+        ceiling=512,
+        capture_bs=_CAPTURE_BS,
+        kv_budget_bytes=int(kv_budget_gib * _GIB),
+        vocab_size=vocab,
+        context_len=_QWEN3_CONTEXT,
+        page_size=1,
+    )
+
+
+class TestGraphBoundedRunningCap(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_qwen3_pools_keep_the_ceiling_on_h100_and_back_off_on_l40s(self):
+        """KV budgets left after Qwen3 weights, net of the post-capture floor. H100
+        pools keep all 512 graphs; the L40S 30B-A3B pool backs off, yet stays above
+        the 128 requests it can hold at 1k-token contexts."""
+        self.assertEqual(_cap(61.66), 512)  # H100, Qwen3-8B
+        self.assertEqual(_cap(47.77), 512)  # H100, Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8
+        l40s_moe = _cap(13.14)
+        self.assertLess(l40s_moe, 512)
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(l40s_moe, 128)
+
+    def test_cap_is_a_captured_size_and_moves_with_the_budget(self):
+        """A captured size needs no extra graph at the request-pool size."""
+        caps = [_cap(gib) for gib in (0.001, 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 1024)]
+        self.assertTrue(all(cap in _CAPTURE_BS for cap in caps), caps)
+        self.assertEqual(caps, sorted(caps))
+        # A tiny pool still serves one request; an ample one keeps the ceiling.
+        self.assertEqual((caps[0], caps[-1]), (1, 512))
+        # A larger vocabulary means a larger per-request reserve, never a larger cap.
+        self.assertLessEqual(_cap(16, vocab=4 * _QWEN3_VOCAB), _cap(16))
+
+
+class TestTransientReserve(CustomTestCase):
+    def _reserve(self, *, requests=512, chunk=8192, deterministic=False, graph_gib=0):
+        return transient_reserve(
+            vocab_size=_QWEN3_VOCAB,
+            max_running_requests=requests,
+            chunked_prefill_size=chunk,
+            enable_deterministic_inference=deterministic,
+            prefill_graph_bytes=int(graph_gib * _GIB),
+        )
+
+    def test_both_tails_stay_reserved_beside_the_sampling_state(self):
+        """512 penalized decodes beside input-logprob prefill chunks made the caching
+        allocator release its cache and retry: blocks freed by one tail were split
+        for the other's tensors. The sampling state, both tails and a stranded block
+        must all fit at once."""
+        slack = self._reserve(requests=0, chunk=0).total_bytes
+        reserve = self._reserve(requests=512, chunk=8192)
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(
+            reserve.total_bytes,
+            slack
+            + reserve.persistent_bytes
+            + reserve.decode_bytes
+            + reserve.prefill_bytes
+            + reserve.fragmentation_bytes,
+        )
+
+    def test_a_logprob_chunk_still_fits_beside_a_stranded_one(self):
+        """An input-logprob prefill under a full penalized decode batch ran out of
+        memory with a whole chunk's worth reserved-but-unallocated: freed chunk
+        blocks were split by smaller per-step tensors. One more chunk must fit."""
+        reserve = self._reserve(requests=208, chunk=4096)
+        chunk_block = 4 * _QWEN3_VOCAB * 2048
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(reserve.fragmentation_bytes, chunk_block)
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(
+            reserve.total_bytes - reserve.persistent_bytes,
+            reserve.prefill_bytes + chunk_block,
+        )
+
+    def test_prefill_tail_covers_an_eager_chunk_and_the_slow_logprob_path(self):
+        """The measured prefill graph pool bounds an eager forward of one chunk, and
+        deterministic inference's full log-softmax holds more than the fast path."""
+        self.assertEqual(self._reserve(graph_gib=64).prefill_bytes, 64 * _GIB)
+        self.assertGreater(
+            self._reserve(deterministic=True).prefill_bytes,
+            self._reserve(deterministic=False).prefill_bytes,
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

@@ -0,0 +1,205 @@
+"""Single-GPU decode CUDA graphs cover more batch sizes than the GPU tier, when and
+only when the graph and memory inputs are left at their defaults. The default plan
+keeps the running limit and reserves for its graphs exactly as the matching explicit
+flag would; sizing the pool after capture caps the default running batch at them.
+
+The planner gates on the final configuration, so the cases resolve the whole
+pipeline over a real config.json rather than calling the hook on a fixture.
+"""
+
+import json
+import os
+import shutil
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+from sglang.srt.arg_groups.overrides import (
+    declare_resolution,
+    post_capture_kv_sizing_planned,
+    resolution_result,
+)
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.cuda_graph_config import Backend
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import override_platform
+from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=30, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+# nvidia-smi memory.total on the single-GPU targets.
+_A10G_MIB = 23028
+_L40S_MIB = 46068
+_H100_MIB = 81559
+
+# Qwen3-8B's attention and vocabulary shape; two layers keep resolution cheap.
+_QWEN3_CONFIG = {
+    "architectures": ["Qwen3ForCausalLM"],
+    "model_type": "qwen3",
+    "hidden_size": 4096,
+    "intermediate_size": 12288,
+    "num_attention_heads": 32,
+    "num_key_value_heads": 8,
+    "head_dim": 128,
+    "num_hidden_layers": 2,
+    "vocab_size": 151936,
+    "max_position_embeddings": 40960,
+}
+
+
+class TestDecodeGraphPlan(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        # Resolution writes environment variables that outlive the record.
+        environment = dict(os.environ)
+
+        def restore():
+            os.environ.clear()
+            os.environ.update(environment)
+
+        self.addCleanup(restore)
+        self.model_path = self._model_dir(_QWEN3_CONFIG)
+
+    def _model_dir(self, config):
+        path = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="decode_graph_plan_")
+        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, path, ignore_errors=True)
+        with open(os.path.join(path, "config.json"), "w") as handle:
+            json.dump(config, handle)
+        return path
+
+    def _resolve(self, gpu_mem=_H100_MIB, *, model_path=None, launcher=None, **fields):
+        """Resolve on a CUDA GPU of ``gpu_mem`` MiB; returns (decode graph config,
+        running cap, post-capture KV sizing planned, mem_fraction_static)."""
+        fields.setdefault("attention_backend", "triton")
+        args = ServerArgs(
+            model_path=model_path or self.model_path, device="cuda", **fields
+        )
+        if launcher:
+            declare_resolution(args, "launcher", **launcher)
+        with (
+            override_platform(is_cuda=True, is_hip=False, is_npu=False, is_xpu=False),
+            patch("sglang.srt.utils.is_cuda", return_value=True),
+            patch(
+                "sglang.srt.arg_groups.memory_hook.get_device_memory_capacity",
+                return_value=gpu_mem,
+            ),
+        ):
+            args.resolve_once()
+            planned = post_capture_kv_sizing_planned(args)
+        return (
+            resolution_result(args, "cuda_graph_config").decode,
+            resolution_result(args, "_decode_graph_running_cap"),
+            planned,
+            resolution_result(args, "mem_fraction_static"),
+        )
+
+    def _resolve_without_planner(self, gpu_mem=_H100_MIB, **kwargs):
+        with envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_DECODE_GRAPH_PLANNER.override(False):
+            return self._resolve(gpu_mem, **kwargs)
+
+    def test_default_plan_per_gpu_tier(self):
+        """Over 60 GiB graphs cover 512 requests, at 35-60 GiB 256; neither caps the
+        running limit, and each reserves what the explicit graph flag reserves.
+        Below 35 GiB the tier plan stays."""
+        for gpu_mem, ceiling, graphs in ((_H100_MIB, 512, 52), (_L40S_MIB, 256, 36)):
+            with self.subTest(gpu_mem=gpu_mem):
+                decode, cap, planned, fraction = self._resolve(gpu_mem)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    (decode.max_bs, len(decode.bs), cap, planned),
+                    (ceiling, graphs, None, False),
+                )
+                explicit = self._resolve(gpu_mem, cuda_graph_max_bs_decode=ceiling)
+                self.assertEqual(fraction, explicit[3])
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._resolve(_A10G_MIB), self._resolve_without_planner(_A10G_MIB)
+        )
+
+    def test_explicit_graph_running_and_memory_flags_keep_their_meaning(self):
+        h100_tier = self._resolve(mem_fraction_static=0.8)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            (h100_tier[0].max_bs, h100_tier[1], h100_tier[2], h100_tier[3]),
+            (256, None, False, 0.8),
+        )
+        # A launcher's fraction is as deliberate as the operator's.
+        launched = self._resolve(launcher={"mem_fraction_static": 0.7})
+        self.assertEqual(
+            (launched[0].max_bs, launched[1], launched[3]), (256, None, 0.7)
+        )
+
+        decode, cap, planned, _ = self._resolve(cuda_graph_max_bs_decode=64)
+        self.assertEqual((decode.max_bs, cap, planned), (64, None, False))
+
+        decode, cap, planned, _ = self._resolve(cuda_graph_bs_decode=[1, 2, 4])
+        self.assertEqual((decode.bs, cap, planned), ([1, 2, 4], None, False))
+
+        decode, cap, _, _ = self._resolve(disable_cuda_graph=True)
+        self.assertEqual((decode.backend, cap), (Backend.DISABLED, None))
+
+        # Only the full decode backend replays every bucket from one graph.
+        decode, cap, _, _ = self._resolve(cuda_graph_backend_decode="breakable")
+        self.assertEqual((decode.backend, decode.max_bs, cap), ("breakable", 256, None))
+
+        # The graphs follow an explicit limit up to the ceiling; above it, decode
+        # stays eager there and the reserve is the explicit graph flag's.
+        decode, cap, planned, _ = self._resolve(_L40S_MIB, max_running_requests=200)
+        self.assertEqual((decode.max_bs, cap, planned), (200, None, False))
+        decode, cap, planned, fraction = self._resolve(max_running_requests=1024)
+        self.assertEqual((decode.max_bs, cap, planned), (512, None, False))
+        explicit = self._resolve(
+            max_running_requests=1024, cuda_graph_max_bs_decode=512
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(fraction, explicit[3])
+
+    def test_post_capture_sizing_bounds_decode_by_its_graphs(self):
+        """With SGLANG_ENABLE_POST_CAPTURE_KV_SIZING, graphs cover 512 requests on
+        any in-scope GPU and cap the default running batch there, so the runtime
+        reserve has a bound; the fraction is the opt-in's post-capture floor."""
+        with envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_POST_CAPTURE_KV_SIZING.override(True):
+            for gpu_mem in (_L40S_MIB, _H100_MIB):
+                with self.subTest(gpu_mem=gpu_mem):
+                    decode, cap, planned, fraction = self._resolve(gpu_mem)
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        (decode.max_bs, len(decode.bs), cap, planned),
+                        (512, 52, 512, True),
+                    )
+                    opt_in = self._resolve(gpu_mem, cuda_graph_max_bs_decode=512)
+                    self.assertEqual(fraction, opt_in[3])
+            decode, cap, planned, _ = self._resolve(max_running_requests=200)
+        self.assertEqual((decode.max_bs, cap, planned), (200, None, True))
+
+    def test_graphs_disabled_after_the_memory_hook_keep_the_tier_plan(self):
+        """torch_native disables CUDA graphs only after the memory heuristic ran; a
+        plan made before that would charge the eager pool for graphs it never has."""
+        plan = self._resolve(attention_backend="torch_native")
+        self.assertEqual((plan[0].backend, plan[1]), (Backend.DISABLED, None))
+        self.assertEqual(
+            plan, self._resolve_without_planner(attention_backend="torch_native")
+        )
+
+    def test_out_of_scope_configs_keep_the_tier_plan(self):
+        """dLLM decode graphs capture block_size tokens per request, and dLLM runs one
+        request unless told otherwise; multi-GPU, unknown memory and the kill switch
+        keep the tier plan as well."""
+        sdar = self._model_dir({**_QWEN3_CONFIG, "architectures": ["SDARForCausalLM"]})
+        for gpu_mem in (_L40S_MIB, _H100_MIB):
+            with self.subTest(dllm_gpu_mem=gpu_mem):
+                dllm = {"model_path": sdar, "dllm_algorithm": "LowConfidence"}
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    self._resolve(gpu_mem, **dllm),
+                    self._resolve_without_planner(gpu_mem, **dllm),
+                )
+
+        decode, cap, planned, _ = self._resolve(tp_size=2)
+        self.assertEqual((decode.max_bs, cap, planned), (256, None, False))
+        decode, cap, planned, _ = self._resolve(gpu_mem=None)
+        self.assertEqual((decode.max_bs, cap, planned), (160, None, False))
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._resolve_without_planner(),
+            self._resolve(cuda_graph_max_bs_decode=256),
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
